items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Advanced degree
6 - 10 years of related experience.
Minimum of 1 year of experience writing and preparing grant proposals and budgets.
Minimum of 1 year of experience developing and applying financial and administrative policies and internal controls.
Experience working in an academic environment and/or in the field of higher education.
Experience in communication (oral and written), leadership and vision.
Demonstrated experience with pre-award and post-award phases of contract and grant administration. Experience in allocating financial resources and preparing interdisciplinary grant proposals.
Previous supervisory/managerial experience.
Supervises the work of a department with responsibility for quality and quantity of work. (25% time)
Participates in the creation, maintenance and reporting of operational and budget processes, academic and/or staff FTE, finance, human resources and space planning. (15% time)

Independently manage and support Institute and Center Directors throughout all pre-award and post-award phases of sponsored projects. Provide guidance and administrative support for proposal development and submission through various electronic research administration systems, including Grants.gov, Cayuse , NSF Fastlane(or successor systems), and the University's Kuali Research platform. Review funding opportunities and assist investigators with proposal preparation, budget development, compliance requirements, and sponsor guidelines. (15% time)

Project Management and Strategic Leadership: Provides analytical and strategic support to the IIGB and Center Directors in developing and implementing the programs, initiatives, events, and goals consistent with the vision and priorities of the Institute. Produces written documents and communications, and forms and serves on implementation committees as appropriate. Writes and acts on behalf of directors and initiates and creates agendas for meeting with faculty fora. Manages and researches all visual and technically written marketing material for online or print display to ensure an integrated program consistent with IIGB's mission and goals. Coordinates fundraising activities and develops materials for priority outreach and engagement. (15% time)
Participates in the development and monitoring of policies and procedures for departmental operations. (10% time)

Exercise independent judgment and discretion in addressing day-to-day operational, financial, and administrative needs of the Institutes and Centers. Proactively identify and anticipate operational, financial, and compliance-related challenges; develop and implement effective solutions in consultation with the Department Financial and Administrative Officer (FAO) and the Directors of IIGB, CEPCEB, and CIVDR. Serve as a trusted advisor to leadership by evaluating issues, assessing risks, and recommending appropriate courses of action to support organizational goals and research initiatives. Keep the Department FAO and Center Directors fully informed of significant operational issues, financial concerns, compliance matters, and proposed resolutions. Coordinate and respond to requests, reporting requirements, and inquiries from the Dean's Office, Accounting, Internal Audit, Extramural Funds Accounting, Contracts & Grants, and other campus administrative units. Ensure departmental activities are conducted in accordance with University policies, sponsor regulations, and established internal procedures. Develop, implement, and continually improve administrative and financial processes to enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness. Represent the Department and Centers in meetings with campus stakeholders and administrative offices regarding financial, research administration, and operational matters. Facilitate communication and collaboration among faculty, staff, campus units, and external sponsors to ensure successful implementation of departmental and research objectives. Monitor administrative operations and recommend strategic improvements to support the long-term financial and operational success of the Institutes and Centers. (10% time)
Recommends hiring of new employees, transfers, promotions, salary actions, terminations, performance management and budget recommendations. (5% time)
May manage systems and procedures to protect departmental assets. (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Constantly

Perform Calculations: Constantly

Bend: Occasionally

Solid knowledge of the organization's processes, protocols and procedures with a focus on budget, account and fund management and/or personnel management within labor contract(s) and personnel policy.
Working knowledge of current University of California (UC) policies and procedures and all applicable laws and regulations.
Solid knowledge of financial analysis and reporting techniques; human resources and risk management planning; accounting and payroll.
Working knowledge of fundraising, donor relations and public relations concepts, principles, procedures and techniques.
Demonstrated skills in employee supervision and HR administration.
Solid knowledge of common organization-specific and other computer application programs.
Solid organizational and customer service skills to effectively manage multiple priorities.
Solid interpersonal skills including verbal and written communication, active listening, critical thinking, persuasiveness, advising, and counseling to effectively motivate others.
Solid skills to quickly evaluate complex issues and identify resolution.
Demonstrated skill in preparing oral and written presentations through various media formats.

Demonstrated skill in MS Office and Google. Extensive experience in creating spreadsheets using Excel with demonstrated knowledge of advanced features. Demonstrated ability to use Adobe and various internet tools.
Skill in reading and understanding complex and/or detailed documents such as proposals, contracts, policies, etc., and guiding the integration of regulations with programmatic needs.
Knowledge of generally accepted accounting principles. Demonstrated experience identifying and analyzing account variances and researching discrepancies.
